paper_style.palette_strategy: Architecture diagrams use pastel semantic blocks; attention uses fixed Fusion 1–4 colors and modality span bands; embeddings use fixed Visual/Audio/Flow categorical colors; performance tables use black/white rules with red/green T-Miss, blue/gray ΔSOTA and bold/underline best markers.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: PDF text, captions, axes and table rules are vector; imported Framework.png and statistical plot bodies are raster or mixed with PDF vector overlays. No plot/table generator source was found in the public repository.
paper_style.style_consistency: The modality and attention families are internally consistent, and all result tables reuse Average/full and ρ/MSE conventions. Figure 1/2 assets and appendix plots use different font/colour lineages, and page-width objects are dense at final scale.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. (a) Reconstruction-based and (b) Distillation/Prior-based incomplete multimodal learning methods typically rely on the unrealistic “full-modal training” assumption to generate missing data or distill priors. In contrast, (c) our LIMSSR leverages the context-aware reasoning capabilities of LLMs to infer latent semantics from available modalities under the more challenging Training-Time Incomplete Observations, eliminating the dependency on complete training data or reconstruction supervision.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. The overall framework of LIMSSR. Given incomplete data, LIMSSR first performs Prompt-Guided Context-Aware Modality Imputation, transforming available modalities into token sequences while using placeholders for missing ones. Guided by structured prompts, an LLM infers latent semantics for missing parts and consolidates multimodal information into fusion tokens. Finally, Mask-Aware Dual-Path Aggregation decodes these representations via uncertainty-calibrated reasoning and cross-modal pattern recovery paths, dynamically weighting them based on missingness states to generate robust scores.

caption.text: Figure 4. Comparative scatter plots illustrating the prediction fidelity of our approach against state-of-the-art baselines, MCMoE (Xu et al., 2026) (incomplete multimodal AQA) and MoMKE (Xu et al., 2024d) (incomplete multimodal emotion recognition), across all modality combinations on the FS1000 (TES) benchmark. figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5. Visualization of the similarity between the semantic representations inferred by LIMSSR and the ground-truth modality representations on the FS1000 test set (TES). (a-c) Display the cosine similarity between the latent semantics inferred by the LLM and the ground-truth representations of all three modalities when the missing modality is Flow, Audio, and Visual, respectively. Each column represents a sample instance, and each row corresponds to a modality. The similarities within each column are normalized to sum to 1. The red dashed box indicates the target missing modality. (d) A bar chart comparison of the similarity between the inferred representation and the target missing modality versus other modalities across the three missingness scenarios. The results indicate that the inferred representations exhibit consistently higher similarity to the target missing modalities, demonstrating that LIMSSR effectively leverages available context to infer useful latent semantics for compensating information loss.

caption.text: Table 1. Comparisons of performance on three benchmarks with incomplete modalities. v, f , and a refer to the RGB, flow, and audio modalities. “Average” denotes the average result of all six incomplete multimodal combinations. caption.text: Table 8. cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 positions training-time incomplete observations; Figure 2 defines PCMI, LLM fusion and MDA; Tables 1–2 establish headline results; Table 3 and Tables 4–8 isolate components; Table 10 adds cost; Figures 3–8 and 9–11 provide attention, fidelity, similarity and embedding mechanisms; Tables 11–13 restore type-level detail.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure 2, Figure 4–6 and Table 1/2/8/9 captions carry substantial setup and encoding definitions. Figure 3 and Figures 9–11 have short captions that rely on panel labels and正文 context; Tables 4–7/10 and 11–13 omit some units, type maps or aggregation details.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Main and expanded result tables reuse Methods × T-Miss × six modality masks × Average × full; ablation tables reuse FS1000/Fis-V Average/full. ρ/MSE pair precision is stable, while assessment abbreviations, cost units and type names are distributed between headers and body text.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 module names map to Table 3 add/remove rows, Table 5 fusion-token K, Table 6 dual paths, Table 7 LoRA and Table 8 prompt deletions; Figure 3/9–11 attention and Figure 5 similarity provide qualitative mechanism checks.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Table 1/2 aggregates are expanded by Tables 11–13; Figure 3 FS1000 attention is expanded by Figures 9–11; Figures 6–8 replicate the representation-alignment grammar over three datasets. Figure 5 remains a detailed FS1000 similarity case rather than a full three-dataset heatmap family.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Serif Nimbus Roman/Times and Computer Modern math dominate PDF prose and tables; sans-serif Calibri-like type dominates plot and architecture labels. The family is consistent within object classes but imported and generated visual assets do not share one exact font source.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Visual/Audio/Flow point colors, Fusion 1–4 attention colors, red/green T-Miss and blue/gray ΔSOTA are reused across object families. Architecture pastels are local semantic roles. Color carries meaningful identity and is only partially redundant in grayscale.

most_reusable_patterns: Page-width architecture showing input masks, prompts/tokens, LLM, dual paths and score/loss in one directional interface.
Fixed modality-mask result schema with Average/full terminal columns, T-Miss markers and ΔSOTA comparison.
Raw-plus-mask qualitative grids for t-SNE and attention, reused across datasets with stable panel order and palette.
Add/remove and path-only/full ablation rows aligned to the method diagram.
Sample-level heatmap paired with scenario-level summary bars for latent-imputation mechanism evidence.
failure_patterns: Page-width tables and 5–8-panel plots are too dense for comfortable final-scale reading.
Figure 3 and Figures 9–11 substantially duplicate attention views without explicit cross-reference or complete condition captions.
Figures 4–8 lack sample denominators, seed/repetition details or uncertainty displays for aggregate/qualitative claims.
Table 10 lacks hardware and measurement protocol, so params/FLOPs do not establish wall-clock cost.
Colour and red/green markers are important semantics but are not fully grayscale-safe.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a high-density strategy in which a page-width architecture defines incomplete-modality reasoning, wide tables close the multi-dataset result surface, and appendix grids, attention plots, embeddings and type-level tables provide mechanism and robustness checks; stronger caption self-containment, grayscale redundancy and uncertainty/denominator reporting would make the evidence easier to audit.
